data.feature_name: OAuth2 JWT Authentication & Session Renewal API
data.summary: Comprehensive test strategy covering core OAuth2 login workflows, JWT lifespan validations, httpOnly cookie security attributes, token rotation mechanics, rate limiting brute-force defense, injection prevention, and CORS policies for Next.js 14 and FastAPI architectures. High security risk profile due to authentication and token handling boundaries.

test_cases.title: Verify successful user login with valid credentials and cookie attributes
test_cases.preconditions: Registered active user account exists in DB (user@example.com / Password123!).
steps: Step 1: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with valid email and password.
Step 2: Inspect HTTP response status code.
Step 3: Validate JSON body schema and access_token properties.
Step 4: Inspect Set-Cookie header for refresh_token parameters.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP status 200 OK. Response body contains { access_token: "<valid_jwt>", token_type: "bearer", expires_in: 900 }. Set-Cookie header sets 'refresh_token' with flags: httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Max-Age=604800 (7 days).

test_cases.title: Validate password field complexity schema and boundary rejection
steps: Step 1: Send POST to /api/v1/auth/login with password < 8 characters ('Pass1!').
Step 2: Send POST with password missing uppercase ('password123!').
Step 3: Send POST with password missing special character ('Password123').
Step 4: Verify response status codes and validation error structures.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP status 422 Unprocessable Entity or HTTP 400 Bad Request for all invalid password attempts. Detailed field validation errors returned without processing credential verification.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: Acceptance Criteria 1: Password validation rules (min 8 chars, 1 uppercase, 1 special char)

test_cases.title: Verify brute-force rate limiting and 30-minute lockout mechanism
test_cases.preconditions: Target user exists and rate limiter cache (e.g., Redis) is initialized.
steps: Step 1: Perform 5 consecutive failed POST /api/v1/auth/login requests using invalid passwords within 15 minutes.
Step 2: Verify HTTP 401 Unauthorized for attempts 1 through 5.
Step 3: Perform 6th POST request with correct valid credentials within the 15-minute window.
Step 4: Check response status code and account lock state.
test_cases.expected_result: 6th attempt returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. User account is locked for 30 minutes, denying even valid credential logins until lockout window expires.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: Acceptance Criteria 1: Rate limiting max 5 failed attempts in 15 mins -> 30 min lock (HTTP 429)

test_cases.title: Verify successful session renewal and refresh token rotation defense
test_cases.preconditions: User logged in; valid non-expired refresh_token cookie stored.
steps: Step 1: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/refresh including valid refresh_token cookie.
Step 2: Check HTTP response status code and JSON body for new access_token.
Step 3: Check Set-Cookie header for updated refresh_token value.
Step 4: Query database to ensure old refresh_token is invalidated/rotated and new token record exists.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP status 200 OK. Returns new access_token. New refresh_token cookie issued. Previous refresh_token is marked revoked/rotated in DB.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: Acceptance Criteria 2: POST /api/v1/auth/refresh token rotation defense

test_cases.title: Reject session renewal request using expired or blacklisted refresh token
test_cases.preconditions: Refresh token is expired (TTL > 7 days) or manually revoked/blacklisted in database.
steps: Step 1: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/refresh with expired or revoked refresh_token cookie.
Step 2: Inspect HTTP status code and response payload.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP status 401 Unauthorized with JSON response { "error": "token_expired_or_revoked" }.

test_cases.title: Verify token reuse detection and breach mitigation during token rotation replay attack
test_cases.preconditions: A valid refresh token (Token A) was refreshed to yield Token B, rendering Token A rotated/invalidated.
steps: Step 1: Replay an already used/rotated refresh token (Token A) in a POST request to /api/v1/auth/refresh.
Step 2: Verify HTTP response status and error body.
Step 3: Inspect user active sessions in DB to ensure session family is revoked.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP status 401 Unauthorized { "error": "token_expired_or_revoked" }. Token reuse alert triggered; all child refresh tokens associated with the compromise chain are invalidated.

test_cases.title: Verify rejection of SQL and NoSQL Injection payloads in authentication requests
test_cases.preconditions: Auth API endpoint running in test environment.
steps: Step 1: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with SQL Injection payload in email field (' OR '1'='1).
Step 2: Send POST request with NoSQL Injection payload in JSON ($gt operator).
Step 3: Verify HTTP status codes and error payloads.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP status 400 Bad Request or 422 Unprocessable Entity. Request is safely rejected without executing malicious query.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: Acceptance Criteria 3: Reject SQL/NoSQL injection payloads with HTTP 400

test_cases.title: Verify strict CORS origin restrictions on authentication endpoints
test_cases.preconditions: FastAPI CORS middleware configured with strict allowed origins list (e.g., https://app.example.com).
steps: Step 1: Send OPTIONS / POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with header Origin: https://malicious-site.com.
Step 2: Inspect Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.
test_cases.expected_result: Access-Control-Allow-Origin header does not match malicious origin or is absent. Next.js/Browser blocks cross-origin credential sharing.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: Acceptance Criteria 3: CORS headers must only allow whitelisted origins

test_cases.title: Verify raw stack trace exposure prevention during unexpected system errors
test_cases.preconditions: Mock internal DB or service failure during POST /api/v1/auth/login.
steps: Step 1: Trigger an unhandled exception or forced DB disconnect during login execution.
Step 2: Inspect HTTP status code and response payload body.
test_cases.test_data: Simulated DB connectivity loss during POST /api/v1/auth/login
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP status 500 Internal Server Error with generic error JSON (e.g., { "error": "internal_server_error" }). Zero traceback, module path, or framework internal leaks present in response body.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: Acceptance Criteria 3: Never expose raw stack traces in error responses

data.suggested_automation_framework: PyTest + HTTPX / Playwright API Testing Context

data.summary: Comprehensive test strategy covering authentication, token lifecycle management, security hardening, and rate limiting in Next.js + FastAPI architecture. Testing focuses on verifying 15-minute access token expiration, 7-day httpOnly refresh cookie rotation, rate-limiting thresholds (5 failed attempts per 15 minutes), and injection vulnerability mitigations. Quality gates enforce 100% pass rate on P0 security and functional automation cases prior to staging/production deployment.

test_cases.title: Verify successful user login with valid credentials issuing 15-min JWT and 7-day httpOnly refresh cookie
test_cases.preconditions: User account exists in FastAPI backend with verified status.
steps: Step 1: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with valid email and password in request body.
Step 2: Inspect response HTTP status code, response body, and response headers.
Step 3: Validate JWT access token claims (exp time set to +15 minutes).
Step 4: Inspect Set-Cookie header for refresh token parameters.
test_cases.expected_result: Status 200 OK. Body contains valid JWT access token expiring in 15 minutes. Set-Cookie header contains refresh token with flags: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Max-Age=604800 (7 days).
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: POST /api/v1/auth/login requires valid email and password. On success returns JWT access token valid 15 mins and httpOnly refresh cookie valid 7 days.

test_cases.title: Verify login rate limiting triggers HTTP 429 after 5 consecutive failed attempts in 15 minutes
test_cases.preconditions: User account exists. Rate limiter cache (e.g., Redis) is cleared for target IP/email.
steps: Step 1: Execute 5 sequential POST requests to /api/v1/auth/login with incorrect password.
Step 2: Verify HTTP 401 status for attempts 1 through 5.
Step 3: Execute 6th POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with correct or incorrect password within 15 minutes.
Step 4: Verify response status code and headers for 6th attempt.
test_cases.expected_result: Attempts 1-5 return HTTP 401 Unauthorized. 6th attempt returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with 'Retry-After' header indicating wait time within the 15-minute window.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: Rate limits to 5 failed attempts per 15 mins.

test_cases.title: Verify refresh token rotation via POST /api/v1/auth/refresh
test_cases.preconditions: User is authenticated and possesses a valid httpOnly refresh cookie.
steps: Step 1: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/refresh attaching valid refresh cookie.
Step 2: Parse response body and Set-Cookie header.
Step 3: Verify new JWT access token is issued with refreshed 15-min expiration.
Step 4: Verify a new httpOnly refresh cookie is returned and old refresh token is invalidated.
test_cases.expected_result: Status 200 OK. New JWT access token issued. Set-Cookie header sets a rotated refresh token cookie. Old refresh token is marked used/invalidated in database/cache.

test_cases.title: Verify SQL Injection resilience in login request parameters
test_cases.preconditions: FastAPI database models connected via ORM/parameterized queries.
steps: Step 1: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with SQL injection payloads in email field.
Step 2: Send POST request with SQL injection payload in password field.
Step 3: Check response status codes and ensure no database syntax errors or unhandled server errors (500) are returned.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 400 Bad Request or HTTP 401 Unauthorized. No authentication bypass occurs. Database error stack traces are never exposed in response body.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: POST /api/v1/auth/login requires valid email and password.

test_cases.title: Verify access token rejection after exact 15-minute expiration window
test_cases.preconditions: JWT access token generated 15 minutes and 1 second ago.
steps: Step 1: Obtain a valid JWT access token.
Step 2: Simulate time progression past 15 minutes (or mock system clock/JWT token exp claim).
Step 3: Send GET request to protected endpoint (e.g., /api/v1/users/me) using Authorization: Bearer <expired_token>.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized with detail 'Token has expired'. Next.js frontend intercepted and triggered automatic refresh flow.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: returns JWT access token valid 15 mins

test_cases.title: Verify detection and prevention of refresh token reuse (Token Family Revocation)
test_cases.preconditions: A refresh token has already been rotated via /api/v1/auth/refresh.
steps: Step 1: Capture Refresh Token A.
Step 2: Call /api/v1/auth/refresh with Token A to receive Refresh Token B.
Step 3: Attempt to call /api/v1/auth/refresh again using the previously invalidated Token A.
Step 4: Verify system revokes Token B and invalidates user session family.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden. The entire token family associated with the compromised token is revoked immediately.

test_cases.title: Verify POST /api/v1/auth/refresh handling with missing or malformed cookie
steps: Step 1: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/refresh without any Cookie header.
Step 2: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/refresh with Cookie: refresh_token=invalid_garbage_string.
test_cases.test_data:
Case A: No cookie header
Case B: Cookie: refresh_token=xyz123malformedjwt
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 401 Unauthorized returned for both requests with explicit error payload (e.g., 'Refresh token missing or invalid').

test_cases.title: Verify rate limiter counter resets after 15-minute cooldown period
test_cases.preconditions: User/IP has reached 5 failed login attempts and is currently rate-limited (429).
steps: Step 1: Trigger 5 failed attempts to lock account rate-limiting counter.
Step 2: Wait 15 minutes (or mock rate limiter TTL expiration).
Step 3: Send POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials.
test_cases.expected_result: HTTP 200 OK. Account successfully authenticates after rate limit window expires, returning new access token and refresh cookie.
test_cases.rag_requirement_ref: Rate limits to 5 failed attempts per 15 mins.

data.suggested_automation_framework: PyTest (with httpx for FastAPI API integration tests) + Playwright Python (for end-to-end Next.js authentication flow validation)
